url_citation.title: Global Ratings?
url_citation.content:
I’ve been selling on Amazon for over 8 years, always proudly maintaining 5 Star ratings, but now I see the new ‘Global Ratings’ that are popping up all over on Amazon listings within the past few months? Example: On one of my best selling products, I only have 21 reviews from actual Amazon buyers, which are all 5 star reviews that I proudly earned by doing things right. Yet I received another 20 ‘Global Ratings’ in the past few weeks and several of them are 4, 3, and 2 star ratings? When I click on the 4, 3, or 2 star option, it reads ‘Sorry, but there are no 4, 3 or 2 star reviews for this product’? Yet in my search, now I only show up as having a 4.5 star rating for that product? Not to mention my sales for that product have gone from around 40 a month to maybe 4 per month since the Global Ratings have shown up on that listing.
I only sell on my own company website and Amazon. I do not sell globally and I have no review option set up on my company website, so does anyone know where these ‘Global Reviews’ are coming from? Is this Amazons way of turning buyers away from third party sellers who have a high rating for their product so customers buy from Amazon instead?
